newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BT to talk when sees way forward.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BT to talk when sees way forward.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Thursday threw its considerable weight behind its American merger partner, MCI Communications Corp, saying it supported the long-distance carrier despite its unexpectedly hefty loss forecasts.

But BT's finance director Robert Brace told Reuters in an interview the group would only comment on a crucial review of MCI's business plans when it could "see the way forward". He confirmed this was likely to take weeks rather than months.

MCI surprised and disappointed BT about three weeks ago by announcing that it was likely to ring losses of $800 million this year in developing its local business and said the deficit was likely to rise next year.

MCI blamed the loss forecasts on foot-dragging of what it called monopolistic local U.S. operators and the slow pace of U.S. local telephone deregulation efforts, which are hampering its plans to expand its local U.S. business.
Brace said BT backed the local investment plans of MCI, which on Wednesday posted a 6.7 percent drop in second-quarter net income to $280 million.

"I think BT is very supportive of MCI and its attempts to develop business in the local business and in its calls for the regulators to open up the markets ...which are basically closed to competition," he said.

BT, which earlier announced higher first quarter pre-tax profits 1.4 percent of 881 million pounds, said it was working with MCI to analyse the facts, understand what was likely to happen and determine the best way forward.
"It isn't a question of checking the books, as such, it's a question of taking a view on what is likely to happen going forward," Brace said.

"But we don't really want to get sucked into any specific comnments because we have agreed that, and it wouldn't be proper," he said. "We're happy to tell people what we have done when we have done it...we don't want to keep talking about it in the meantime."

BT, which is looking abroad to help boost growth amid increasing competition at home, has been under pressure by institutional investors to re-negotiate the merger terms in the light of rising earnings dilution because of MCI's delays in breaking further into local markets.
And some investors are growing increasingly impatient at what they see as a news blackout ahead of the strategic review's completion.

BT's first quarter pre-tax profits, which came in above analyst forecasts, were flattered by a lower-than-expected redundancy charge of 16 million pounds and a 20 million pound exceptional profit on sales.

But the group said rising competition at home, the start-up costs of European joint ventures ahead of European liberalisation next year and a lower contribution from MCI, of 35 million pounds, all helped to keep a lid on profits.
